msContents.summary: Greek-Latin bilingual of the Pauline epistles.

projectDesc.p: This transcription was made by the COMPAUL Project, funded between 2011-16 by a Starting Grant awarded to Dr H.A.G. Houghton under the European Union Seventh Framework Programme (FP7/2007-13 grant agreement 283302).

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was made on a Vulgate base text, from a colour PDF at . Reference was also made to the 1909 facsimile for pages which have suffered water damage. This is a bilingual manuscript with Latin glosses above the Greek text; only the Latin has been transcribed. This transcription includes all corrections, page layout information, formatting, punctuation, abbreviations and digraphs. Punctuation is practically non-existent in the Latin line and there is no rubrication of the Latin text, only the larger Greek capitals (where it has been added later). Unless otherwise indicated, word divisions correspond to the Vulgate base text. The transcriber was Christina Kreinecker in April 2012 and the transcription was proofread against the same source by Hugh Houghton in April 2017.

As with other epistles in this manuscript, alternative readings (signified by alt) and glosses (signified by gl) have been added, many by the first hand but possibly not at the first time of writing. In some cases, the alternative is found in front of the original or principal reading and has been tagged as such (this is normally indicated by the fact that the original reading appears immediately above the corresponding Greek and the preceding text is displaced). Accents are added above certain Latin vowels; generally this is not easily confused with abbreviations, apart from the case of sic above ουτως (as sicut is normally written plene above καθως).
The plain text file was converted to XML in February 2018. The original transcription guidelines can be found at
The XML specifications used are version 1.5 of the IGNTP Guidelines available at
